historic_survey.survey: Inner Mission North Context Statement, adopted 2004
historic_survey.eligible_district: Mission Reconstruction District; Inner Mission Commercial Corridor
historic_survey.note: Contributor to the Mission Reconstruction District locally significant area (250 Valencia St). Criterion C: the survey's proposed district for the northern Mission's rebuilding after the 1906 earthquake and fire, period of significance May 1906–1913, predominantly Classical Revival, Edwardian and Mission Revival in wood frame construction. Contributor to the Inner Mission Commercial Corridor locally significant area (250 Valencia). Formerly called the 16th Street Commercial Corridor. Criterion C: San Francisco's largest concentration of residential-over-commercial and small-scale commercial buildings, spanning both pre-1906 and post-disaster construction, dated c. 1870s–1931. Named among the survey's properties of individual significance (Levi Strauss & Co. factory). Listed among the designated resources found in the survey area as Levi Strauss & Co. factory.

building.name: Levi Strauss & Co. factory
building.completed_conflict: The Market & Octavia context statement describes a building of 1906 at this address; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1907.

historical_record.description: Designed by the San Francisco architect Albert Pissis for Levi Strauss & Co.: a heavy-timber frame, wood-clad, single-use industrial building of a kind rarely built in San Francisco after the earthquake, and possibly the only one of its size. Dated 1907.
Listed in the city directory as Levi Strauss & Co.
Photographed, showing the Levi Strauss and Company.

Designated a City Structure of Merit. One of the 148 industrial buildings the survey inventoried as standing in its Industrial Employment Study Area, the mixed industrial and residential district between Market, Howard, 16th and 9th streets.

Named as the most notable of the light industrial spaces in the Mission Dolores neighbourhood after the 1906 earthquake and fire — the shirt and overall manufacturer Levi Strauss, on the block between Clinton Park and Brosnan Street.
